title: How round can you draw a circle by hand?
description: Five artwork pictures are made of circles that touch, share a middle spot or overlap. The video reads each picture, draws the circles and checks how even a hand drawn circle really is. Keeko raises the doubt that freehand circles look round enough.
teaching_notes: One idea: a circle drawn by hand comes out uneven. Watch for the slip of thinking a wobbly circle is good enough, which makes an instrument for drawing circles seem unnecessary.

source: Look at five artwork pictures made of circles and try drawing them freehand
video_script.why: The child reads how circles sit in a picture and sees for themselves that a freehand circle is uneven.
video_script.substitution: Lay the freehand circle over the picture circle and look at the gaps.
video_script.anchor: The five artwork pictures of the book, each made of circles
video_script.wrong_answer: the freehand circles look round enough
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks a wobbly circle drawn by hand is good enough. Laying it over the picture circle shows gaps and thick places.
video_script.payoff_line: A circle drawn by hand comes out uneven.

final_answer.value: round circles in the right places and sizes; freehand circles come out uneven
final_answer.spoken: a correct drawing has round circles in the right places and sizes, and a circle drawn by hand comes out uneven

maths_rules: Picture 1: two circles of the same size touch at one place.
Picture 2: two circles share one middle spot; the inner one is about half the size of the outer one.
Picture 3: three equal circles in a row, each overlapping the next.
Mouse face: 1 big circle for the face + 2 ears + 2 eyes = 5 circles, plus a dot and a short line.
Last picture: two crossing lines with a small circle at the bottom end of each line.
A freehand circle drifts inside the picture circle in one place and outside in another, so it is uneven.
video_script.design: One idea: circles are read by how they touch, share a middle spot or overlap, and a hand cannot draw them evenly. Assumes nothing. Wrong idea: freehand is good enough. The pictures stay all video.
